evidence.quote: further gradual increases in the federal funds rate are likely to be appropriate and most conducive to meeting and maintaining those objectives
In that context, this past Friday's labor market report was disappointing.
Inflation has run persistently below the Fed's goal of 2 percent over the past several years even as the labor market strengthened significantly.
If inflation expectations really are moving lower, that could call into question whether inflation will move back to 2 percent as quickly as I expect.
if inflation were to remain persistently low or the expansion were to falter, the FOMC would be able to provide only a limited amount of additional stimulus through conventional means.
I view our modestly accommodative stance of policy as appropriate for several reasons.

parsed.rationale: The speech is Yellen-style: it reaffirms conditional gradual rate increases, but it stresses the weak May jobs report, below-target inflation, falling inflation expectations and asymmetric risks at the lower bound. These cautious points roughly offset the tightening signal, leaving a balanced to slightly dovish net stance.
